title: Aviation (US)
toggle.airspace: Class B, C and D airspace
notCoveredNote: FAA data covers only the United States and its territories, so this area has no aviation detail.
dataNote: FAA aeronautical data. Decorative only: not for navigation.
dataNoteWithCycle: FAA aeronautical data, cycle {cycle}. Decorative only: not for navigation.
lineStyleNote: Class B is drawn heavier, Class D dashed and special use airspace hatched on the inside, each in its own SVG group. Symbols follow the VFR sectional legend.
airspaceIn3dNote: Builds the airspace over the model as acrylic pieces standing on rods above the terrain.
buildNote.layered: Acrylic at each altitude where airspace starts or ends
buildNote.solid: Every sheet from floor to ceiling
levelNote.plates: All the airspace at that height
levelNote.tiers: Just the steps of the wedding cake
formNote.plates: Each level is cut to all the airspace at its height, shelves frosted. Sturdy, and through rods pass several levels. Open air between levels. The two differ most where special use airspace spans several levels; over a single Class B they look much alike.
formNote.tiers: Each level holds only the shelves that start or end there, the chart guide's wedding cake. The least acrylic; more rods. Open air between levels. The two differ most where special use airspace spans several levels; over a single Class B they look much alike.
formNote.volumes: Every acrylic sheet from floor to ceiling, stacked solid. Uses far more acrylic than layered airspace.
classDNote: A flat lid over each tower airport
capAtHighestCeiling: Cap at the highest Class B or C ceiling
rodJointNote.through: One rod per column stands in the terrain and rises through holes in the pieces; you glue each piece at the height the guide gives.
rodJointNote.segments: A short rod between each level, glued on the outline engraved on the piece below. The guide lists every length.
noAirspaceHere: There is no airspace here: FAA data covers the US and its territories.
stackSummary: {pieces, plural, one {# piece} other {# pieces}} on {levels, plural, one {# level} other {# levels}}, {height} {unit} tall{rods, plural, =0 {} one {, held by # rod ({rodLength} {unit} in all)} other {, held by # rods ({rodLength} {unit} in all)}}.{backing, select, yes { Some rods go through the bottom layer onto a backing sheet, which exports with the airspace.} other {}}
levelsMerged: Some airspace levels are too close to separate at this exaggeration. A whole Class B separates near {value}×.
assemblyNote: Pieces sit at true height on rods you cut to the lengths in the assembly guide, exported as separate files. Not for navigation.
